premises.text: Language barriers in daily life need better solutions than machine translation/algorithms
premises.evidence_span: we had A big problem with language barriers. Working, talking day to day, going to the doctor

premises.text: Babelverse crowdsources real-time human interpreters globally for live video and conferences
premises.evidence_span: it's crowdsourcing of real-time human interpreters all around the globe

premises.text: Interpreter profiles capture languages, levels, dialects/accents, availability windows, and domain expertise
premises.evidence_span: we collect the dialects and the accents too

premises.text: Hybrid professional-plus-crowd supply with training/rating ladder aims to cover ~7,000 spoken languages
premises.evidence_span: this is a hybrid crowdsource kind of solution. So we have professionals

premises.text: Long-term: anyone can travel and converse in native languages via human-powered Babel-fish style communication
premises.evidence_span: you can travel anywhere in the world and be able to speak with anybody regardless of what language they speak or what you speak

value.text: Real-time human interpretation so people communicate across languages with emotion and context, not Globish
value.evidence_span: Everybody can speak their native language and understand each other

causal_links.evidence_span: there must be a better way than machine translation
you should hear an interpreter interpreting what I'm saying in real time into Spanish
Babelverse can bring a revolution in communications

notes: Machine-translation inadequacy as problem. Live video product, profile matching (dialect/expertise/availability), and hybrid pro/crowd ladder folded as supply-platform cascade (§4.1.7). Tsunami use coded as application evidence of mechanism not separate premise. Babel-fish travel vision coded as stated market-acceptance condition for the theory (§4.1.4 borderline—kept as GTM/outcome premise). Traction count ~3000 excluded as metric. Three domains.
